sources.locator: "1982 invasion of the Falkland Islands", revision 1372863686, lead

explanation: The invasion's own lead states it in one sentence: "The invasion served as a catalyst for the subsequent Falklands War." The word the article chooses is catalyst and not cause, which is why this is `probable` and not `consensus`; rule 22 would refuse `consensus` on a Wikipedia citation in any case. The edge is written beside the filing and not instead of it: the invasion is also part of the war, and in this atlas `parent` is a display fact that never enters the adjacency, so saying that the landing of 2 April set off what followed is an argument the graph has to carry on its own.
